31-009.r: Distribution of legislative powers between Centre and States (Union, State, Concurrent Lists) → Seventh Schedule; Article 246.

31-010.r: Concurrent List → both Union and States can make laws; if the two laws conflict, the Union law prevails.

31-011.r: Economic and social planning; infants and minors → Concurrent List → both Central and State Governments can make laws.

31-012.r: Residuary legislative powers → Parliament (Article 248); in the USA they rest with the States.
31-012.t: Don't confuse India's model with the USA, where residuary powers go to the States.

31-013.r: Residuary subjects → matters not in any of the three Lists (Union, State, Concurrent); only Parliament can legislate on them (Article 248).

31-014.r: Residuary powers vested in the Union Government (Parliament) → shows India as a federation with a strong Union.

31-015.r: Article 249 → Parliament can make laws on any State List subject in the national interest.

31-016.r: Article 249(1) resolution of the Council of States → Parliament's law on a State subject stays in force for not more than one year [Art 249(2)].

31-017.r: Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 (Parliament to legislate on a State subject in national interest) → in force for not more than one year.
31-017.h: 249 = Rajya Sabha's '1-year pass' to the State List.

31-018.r: Article 263 → Inter-State Council to coordinate Centre-State and inter-state relations; established by the President; its source is the Constitution.

31-021.r: Inter-State Council → set up by the President (Art 263) by order of 28 May 1990; PM chairs; CMs of all states and six Union Cabinet ministers are members.

31-022.r: Inter-State Council → Article 263; constituted by President's order (first in May 1990); PM is head, with six Union Cabinet ministers and all Chief Ministers.

31-023.r: Extra-constitutional, extra-legal bodies → National Development Council and Governors' Conference. Zonal Councils → statutory (Act of Parliament); Inter-State Council → constitutional (Art 263).

31-024.r: Zonal (regional) Councils → made by Parliamentary law (Act of 1956): five councils (North, South, Central, East, West); North East council 1971; Union Home Minister chairs each.

31-026.r: Zonal Councils → statutory advisory bodies (States Reorganisation Act, 1956), not constitutional; five set up originally; Chandigarh included though not a state.
31-026.t: Don't confuse: Inter-State Council is constitutional; Zonal Councils are statutory.

31-027.r: Regional (Zonal) Councils → act as 'Sub-Federal Links' of Indian federalism and promote cooperation and integration among states; both statements correct.

31-028.r: North Eastern Council (Act 1971, amended 2002) → Governors and CMs of member states + three members nominated by President; Home Minister is not a listed member.
31-028.t: Home Minister heads NEC only as President's nominee chairman, not as an ex-officio member under the Act.

31-029.r: Jharkhand Area Autonomous Council → formed 8 August 1995; covered 18 districts of Santhal Pargana and Chota Nagpur.

31-030.r: National Integration → political, economic, social, cultural and psychological dimensions (A true). National Integration Council formed 1962, not 1961 (R false).

31-031.r: Wrong pair: River Boards Act → 1956, not 1970. Correct: Art 262 (Parliament on inter-state water disputes), Inter-State Water Disputes Act 1956, National Water Policy 1987.
31-031.h: Both water Acts share 1956: River Boards Act and Inter-State Water Disputes Act.

31-032.r: Sarkaria Commission → review of Union-State relations; set up 9 June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria; other members B. Shivaraman and Dr. S.R. Sen.

31-034.r: Sarkaria Commission (Centre-State relations) report year is none of 1983, 1984, 1985, 1987 → 'None of the above'; BPSC's key (d) was wrong.
31-034.h: Set up in 1983; report came in January, after all the listed years.

31-036.r: Sarkaria Commission → Article 356 (President's Rule) to be used sparingly, only in rare cases, because ruling parties at the Centre misused it; A and R true, R explains A.

31-037.r: Sarkaria Commission → recommended a permanent Inter-State Council called 'Inter-Governmental Council'; ISC formed May 1990 under Art 263, headed by PM.

31-038.r: Inter-Governmental Council (a permanent Inter-State Council under Art 263) → recommended by Sarkaria Commission (1983-88), not Rajmannar or Punchhi.

31-039.r: Inter-State Council set up on recommendation of Sarkaria Commission (1983, Justice R.S. Sarkaria) as a permanent national forum under Art 263.

31-040.r: Only Inter-State Council is constitutional (Art 263). National Security Council → executive decision; Zonal Councils → statutory (ordinary Act of Parliament).

31-041.r: Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) → state funding of elections, not Centre-State relations. Sarkaria, Rajmannar, Punchhi → Centre-State relations.
31-041.h: Indrajit Gupta → 'gupt daan' (secret donation) → links to election funding.
hi: State funding of elections (चुनावों का राजकीय वित्तपोषण)

31-042.r: Demand to review Centre-State relations grows because States lack adequate resources for development and depend on the Centre; A and R true, R explains A.

31-043.r: Article 256 → State executive power must ensure compliance with Parliament's laws; Union can give States necessary directions; A and R true, R explains A.

31-044.r: Article 257 → State executive power must not impede or prejudice Union executive power; Union may give directions to States for this.

31-045.r: Centre-State financial relations → Part XII (Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits). Part XI = Union-State relations; Part X = Scheduled and Tribal Areas; Part XIII = trade and commerce.

31-046.r: Union-State financial relations (distribution of revenues, grants-in-aid, Finance Commission) → Articles 268 to 281.

31-047.r: Article 270 → taxes levied and collected by the Centre but distributed between Centre and States, e.g., tax on income other than agricultural income.

31-048.r: Art 270 → taxes levied and collected by Union, shared with States: now all Union List taxes except those under Arts 268, 269 and 269A.
31-048.c: No answer printed; by the explanation's rule, more than one option (corporation tax, non-agricultural income tax, customs) fits.

31-049.r: Stamp duty on financial documents (Art 268) → imposed by Union, collected and appropriated by States; so neither 'imposed by State' nor 'regulated by Union' is correct.

31-050.r: Taxes on stock-exchange and futures-market transactions → Union List; levied and collected by Union (proceeds to States) → only 'levied by Union' is correct.

31-051.r: Land Revenue → tax exclusively imposed and collected by States (State List, entry 45). Income tax, corporation tax → Union.

31-052.r: Discretionary grants by Union (or State) for any public purpose → Article 282.

31-053.r: A State cannot take foreign loans directly; Art 293(1) → States borrow only within India on security of their Consolidated Fund, within limits set by State Legislature.

31-054.r: Agricultural income tax → assigned to States by the Constitution itself (State List entry 46; Art 274).

31-055.r: Fiscal disputes between Centre and States → settled by Supreme Court (Art 131); Finance Commission only recommends tax sharing.
31-055.t: Don't pick Finance Commission: it recommends tax sharing, it does not settle disputes.

31-056.r: Tax on professions, trades, callings and employments → Constitution caps it at Rs 2,500 per person per year [Art 276(2)]; raised from Rs 250 by 60th Amendment, 1988.

31-057.r: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India → Article 301 (Part XIII).

31-058.r: Article 300 → suits and proceedings: Government of India sues or is sued as 'Union of India'; a State Government as the State.

32-001.r: Three emergencies → National Emergency (Art 352), President's Rule on failure of state constitutional machinery (Art 356), Financial Emergency (Art 360).
32-001.h: 352, 356, 360 → Nation, State, Money: each four apart.

32-002.r: Art 355 → Union's duty to protect States from external aggression and internal disturbance; Art 352 → National Emergency.
32-002.t: Don't confuse Art 355 (Union's duty to protect States) with Art 356 (President's Rule).

32-005.r: National Emergency (Art 352) grounds → war, external aggression, armed rebellion; 'internal disturbance' replaced by 'armed rebellion' (44th Amendment, 1978). Communal clashes not a ground.

32-008.r: President can declare Emergency for external aggression (Art 352), failure of state constitutional machinery (Art 356) and financial crisis (Art 360); internal disturbance no longer a ground.

32-011.r: National Emergency (Art 352) → President acts only on Union Cabinet's decision communicated in writing [Art 352(3)].
32-011.t: Not 'Prime Minister' or 'Council of Ministers': the written advice must come from the Union Cabinet.

32-012.r: A: Art 352 deals with declaring Emergency (true). R: emergency can arise any time, even on imminent danger (true), but R does not explain A.

32-013.r: Proclamation of (National) Emergency → Article 352 (war, external aggression, armed rebellion, or imminent danger); Art 356 → failure of constitutional machinery in a state.

32-014.r: National Emergency (Art 352) → proclaimed by President; approved by Parliament within 1 month (earlier two months, cut by 44th Amendment 1978); special majority (2/3); revoked by simple majority.

32-015.r: Emergency proclamation (Art 352) → must be approved by both Houses within one month, or it ceases to operate.

32-017.r: Tax-sharing provisions (Arts 268 to 281) → President's order can suspend or modify them during National Emergency [Art 354(1)].

32-018.r: Art 359 → President can suspend enforcement of Fundamental Rights except Arts 20 and 21. Art 358 → Art 19 suspended on war or external aggression (after 44th Amendment).
32-018.t: Don't confuse Art 358 (Art 19 suspended automatically) with Art 359 (President's order suspending enforcement of FRs).

32-019.r: Emergency → Art 19 auto-suspended (Art 358, war/external aggression); President can suspend other FRs incl. Art 21A (Art 359); Arts 20 and 21 never suspended.
32-019.c: No single answer: options (c) Art 21-A and (d) Art 19 are both correct, so the Commission excluded the question.

32-022.r: During National Emergency, Lok Sabha term → extendable by Parliament by law, one year at a time, not beyond six months after Emergency ends [Art 83(2)].

32-023.r: During Emergency, State Legislative Assembly term → extended by Parliament by law [Art 172(1)], one year at a time, up to six months after Emergency ends.

32-024.r: Emergency on 'internal disturbance' → 25 June 1975 by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed (Art 352); withdrawn 21 March 1977; 44th Amendment 1978 replaced it with 'armed rebellion'.

32-025.r: Indian Constitution → federal with unitary elements (statement true). Failure of state constitutional machinery → Art 356, not Art 352 (reason false).
32-025.t: Don't confuse Art 352 (National Emergency) with Art 356 (President's Rule in a State).

32-026.r: President's Rule in a State → Article 356; imposed mainly on the Governor's report, though the President can act otherwise too.

32-028.r: Governor's Rule → only in old Jammu and Kashmir (Section 92 of its own Constitution; Art 370 status), besides President's Rule (Art 356). Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya had none.
32-028.c: No answer printed: three options (Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya) fit, so the UP Commission did not evaluate it.

32-029.r: President's Rule (Art 356) → State Legislature's powers exercised by or under authority of Parliament; Assembly suspended or dissolved, not automatically dissolved; Fundamental Rights (Art 19) unaffected.

32-030.r: President's Rule → State Council of Ministers is removed; dissolution of the Assembly and of local bodies are not necessary consequences (Assembly may be suspended).

32-031.r: S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994) → Art 356 proclamation open to judicial review; failure must be real; Assembly not dissolved until both Houses approve within two months.

32-032.r: President's Rule → maximum three years by successive Parliament resolutions; beyond one year only if National Emergency operates and Election Commission certifies polls impossible (44th Amendment, 1978).

32-033.r: President's Rule imposed till 2019 → Manipur 10, Uttar Pradesh 9, Bihar 8, Odisha 6 times.

32-034.r: President's Rule (Art 356) → first used in Punjab in 1951; then PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) in 1953, the earliest among the options.

32-035.r: Financial Emergency (Art 360) → lapses after 2 months unless both Houses approve; President can order salary cuts for Union and State staff, including Supreme Court and High Court judges.
32-035.t: Statement 2 was wrong only because it excluded the judges; their salaries can also be cut.

32-036.r: Financial Emergency (Art 360) → President can order salary cuts for State employees and Union employees incl. SC/HC judges; State money bills reserved for President only if he so directs.
32-036.c: No answer printed; only statements 1 and 3 are correct, and no option gives that pair.

32-037.r: Article 360 (Financial Emergency) → never used so far; Articles 352 and 356 have been used.
32-037.h: Art 360, like 360 degrees, brings you back to zero: zero uses.

32-038.r: Financial Emergency (Art 360) → never declared in India so far.

32-039.r: "Emergency power of the President is a fraud with the Constitution" → K.M. Nambiar, while opposing President's Rule provisions.

33-001.r: Finance Commission (Art 280) → set up by President every fifth year; recommends sharing of net tax proceeds between Union and States; first one 6 April 1952 under K.C. Neogy.

33-007.r: Principles for sharing revenue between Union and States → Finance Commission, constituted every 5 years. Inter-State Council → coordination; Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) → resource allocation.

33-011.r: Qualifications of Finance Commission members → fixed by Parliament (Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951), not the President (A false); President appoints Chairman and members (R true).

33-012.r: Qualifications and manner of selection of Finance Commission members → determined by Parliament by law [Art 280(2)].
33-012.t: President appoints the members, but Parliament fixes their qualifications.

33-014.r: Finance Commission → Chairman + four other members (not six); reports to the President [Art 280(3)], not to NITI Aayog → neither statement correct.

33-015.r: Finance Commission → divides net tax proceeds among States; sets principles for grants-in-aid. Not its job: withdrawal from Consolidated Fund (Parliament) or checking tax collection (Finance Ministry).

33-018.r: Finance Commission [Art 280(3)] → tax sharing, grants-in-aid (Art 275), funds for Panchayats and municipalities, matters referred by President; not foreign capital, PSU finances or transparency.

33-019.r: Federal Finance Commission → finances between the Centre and the States; it recommends distribution of finance between Union and States.

33-021.r: 12th Finance Commission (2005 to 2010) → Dr. C. Rangarajan, former RBI Governor. 13th → Vijay Kelkar; 14th (2015-2020) → Y.V. Reddy.
33-021.h: 12th → Rangarajan, the RBI Governor: R for Rangarajan and Reserve Bank.

33-022.r: Finance Commission chairmen: 13th → Vijay Kelkar; 14th → Y.V. Reddy (formed January 2013); 15th → N.K. Singh (constituted 27 November 2017).
33-022.c: The explanation stops at the 15th Commission; a sixteenth (chair Arvind Panagariya) has since been set up. The count keeps rising, so none of the options fits now.

33-025.r: 15th Finance Commission → Chairman N.K. Singh; constituted 27 November 2017 under Art 280; two reports: for 2020-21 and for 2021-26.

33-026.r: Finance Commission → a Chairman and four other members [Art 280(1)], appointed by the President.
33-026.h: 1 + 4 = a five-member body, set up every five years.

33-027.r: Article 281 → the President causes every Finance Commission recommendation to be laid before each House of Parliament.

33-028.r: State Finance Commission → constitutional (Art 243-I; set up by Governor every fifth year; Seventy-Third Amendment, 1992) (A true). Union Finance Commission does cover Panchayats [Art 280(3)(bb)] (R false).

33-029.r: State Finance Commission → a constitutional body, constituted by the Governor under Article 243-I.

34-001.r: Planning Commission (March 1950, Nehru) → abolished by PM Narendra Modi (announced 15 August 2014); NITI Aayog set up 1 January 2015 by Union Cabinet resolution.

34-004.r: NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson → appointed by the Prime Minister (Cabinet Minister rank); first was Dr. Arvind Pangariya (January 2015 to August 2017); PM is ex-officio chairman.

34-006.r: NITI Aayog Governing Council → PM (chair), CMs of all States, CMs of Delhi and Puducherry, Lt. Governors of other UTs; Governors of States not included.

34-007.r: Planning Commission → set up 15 March 1950 by Union Cabinet resolution (non-constitutional). NITI Aayog → also extra-constitutional, from 1 January 2015.

34-011.r: Planning Commission → not a constitutional body (executive order, 1950). UPSC and State PSCs (Art 315) and Finance Commission (Art 280) are constitutional.

34-015.r: Not in the Constitution → National Development Council (1952) and Planning Commission (1950), both by executive order; Zonal Councils, statutory (States Reorganisation Act, 1956).

34-016.r: First Chairman of Planning Commission → Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, as the Prime Minister was its ex-officio Chairman (set up 15 March 1950).

34-019.r: NITI Aayog → came 1 January 2015 to replace Planning Commission; works on cooperative federalism; has no full-time Chairman (PM is ex-officio Chairperson).
34-019.t: The false statement is 'full-time Chairman'; the PM heads it ex officio.

34-020.r: NITI Aayog → Chairperson is Narendra Modi, as the Prime Minister is its ex-officio Chairman; set up 1 January 2015 in place of Planning Commission.

34-021.r: Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission → rank of a Cabinet Minister; first Deputy Chairman was Gulzarilal Nanda.

34-023.r: Never Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission → P. Chidambaram. Were: Dr. Manmohan Singh (1985-1987), Pranab Mukherjee (1991-1996), Montek Singh Ahluwalia (2004-2014).

34-024.r: Planning Commission → called 'Economic Cabinet' of Union and States (extra-constitutional powers, wide scope); it formulated five-year plans; both true, but R does not explain A.

34-025.r: Merger of Finance Commission and Planning Commission → suggested by M.V. Mathur, a member of the 3rd Finance Commission (1960).

34-027.r: Wrong statement: Planning Commission was the highest planning body. Apex body → National Development Council, presided by PM; Planning Commission Secretary is NDC Secretary.

34-028.r: NDC → gives guidelines for the National Plan, considers it, reviews progress and suggests ways to meet its goals; allocating money was the Planning Commission's job.

34-030.r: NDC members → PM (Chairman), Union Cabinet ministers, CMs of all states, CMs/Administrators of UTs, Planning Commission (NITI Aayog) members; not the Finance Commission Chairman.

34-031.r: NDC → final approval of five-year plans; set up 6 August 1952 by executive order; PM presides; Planning Commission Secretary is its Secretary; coordinates Planning Commission and States.

34-035.r: NDC → non-constitutional and non-statutory (so 'statutory body' is wrong); meets at least twice a year; PM heads it; CMs of all states are members.

35-001.r: Lokpal Selection Committee (Act 2013) → PM (chair), Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, CJI or his nominee SC judge, one eminent jurist; no Rajya Sabha Chairman.
35-001.h: Only Lok Sabha figures sit on it: Lokpal goes with Lok Sabha.

35-002.r: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 → no Rajya Sabha Chairman on Selection Committee (1 false); applies to public servants within and outside India [Sec 1(3)] (2 true).

35-003.r: Lokpal Chairperson/Member → minimum age 45 (only true statement). Covers public servants in and outside India; Chairperson need not be CJI; PM is within its jurisdiction.

35-004.r: First Lokpal of India → Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose (retired SC judge); Lokpal and Lokayukta first proposed by Administrative Reforms Commission (1966-1970).

35-005.r: Lokpal Chairperson in 2024 → Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar (assumed office 10 March 2024); first was Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose.

35-006.r: Lokpal and Lokayukta → recommended by first Administrative Reforms Commission (set up 5 January 1966 under Morarji Desai; K. Hanumanthaiah from 1967; ended 1970).

35-008.r: Indian Ombudsman → Lokpal; Ombudsman began in Sweden (1809). First ARC (Morarji Desai) recommended Lokpal, Lokayukta and a Local Body Ombudsman.
35-008.h: Ombudsman is a Swedish idea: Sweden, 1809.

35-011.r: First Lokpal Bill → 1968 (4th Lok Sabha); passed by Lok Sabha in 1969 but lapsed when Lok Sabha was dissolved.

35-012.r: Lokpal Bill 2011 → introduced in Lok Sabha 4 August 2011 by V. Narayanaswami (not P. Chidambaram); sent to Standing Committee; civil society called it 'weak'. Law: 1 January 2014.

35-013.r: Civil society members on Lokpal Bill drafting panel → Anna Hazare, Arvind Kejariwal, Shanti Bhushan, N. Santosh Hegde, Prashant Bhushan.
35-013.t: Trap names: 'Prashant Joshi' (real member Prashant Bhushan) and Kiran Bedi, who was not on the panel.

35-014.r: First Lokayukta → Maharashtra (1972); then Bihar (1973), Uttar Pradesh (1975). Odisha passed the first Lokayukta law (body only in 1983) and first abolished it (1993).

35-015.r: First Lokayukta → Maharashtra (Act 1971; in effect 25 October 1972). Governor appoints Lokayukta on CM's advice for five years.
35-015.t: Don't confuse: Odisha passed the first Lokayukta Act, but Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta.

35-016.r: First Lokayukta institution → Maharashtra, under the Maharashtra Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1971.

35-017.r: Uttar Pradesh Lokayukta → submits its report to the Governor (UP Lokayukta Act, 1975); report laid before both Houses of the State Legislature.

35-018.r: Uttar Pradesh Lokayukta tenure → 5 years or age 70, whichever earlier, from 26 February 2024 (amended Act of 1975); earlier it was 8 years.
35-018.c: Printed (a) 5 years follows the February 2024 amendment; when asked (2017) the tenure was 8 years, option (d).

35-019.r: First state to pass the Lokayukta Bill in 2011 → Uttarakhand (1 November 2011).

35-020.r: Chief Minister under Lokayukta Act → Madhya Pradesh and Orissa when asked; now also Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab and others.

35-021.r: Rajasthan Lokayukta Act, 1973 (Section 7) → corruption and misconduct of ministers and public servants. Sexual harassment, caste discrimination, violence against children → police (SC/ST Act, POCSO), not Lokayukta.

35-022.r: Narpat Mal Lodha Committee (2014, Rajasthan) → review of the Lokayukta Act. Lokpal and Lokayukta Act, 2013 came into force 16 January 2014.

35-023.r: 'Minority' is not defined in the Constitution (A true); Minority Commission is statutory (National Minority Commission Act, 1992), not constitutional (R true), but R does not explain A.

35-024.r: National Commission for Minorities → statutory (Act of 1992, in force 17 May 1993). Minorities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Zoroastrians; Jains added 27 January 2014. Constitution protects religious, linguistic minorities.
35-024.c: Printed answer (d) includes statement 1, which the explanation calls false now (six communities since 2014); it fitted only when asked in 2001.

35-025.r: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities → Art 350B, added by 7th Amendment, 1956 (not 9th); one officer at Union level appointed by President, not one per State.

35-026.r: Functions of National Commission for Women → Section 10 of the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 (enforced 30 August 1990).

35-027.r: Secondary Education Commission (1952-53) → Chairman Dr. A. Laxman Swami Mudaliar, VC of Madras University; called 'Mudaliar Commission'.

35-028.r: Not in existence now → Planning Commission (15 March 1950), replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015. NCW, Minority Commission and NHRC still exist.

35-029.r: Vohra Committee (1993) → nexus of criminals, politicians and bureaucrats (criminalisation of politics).

35-031.r: Ending of IAS and IPS (All India Services) → recommended by Rajamannar Commission.

35-032.r: UDHR (1948) reflected beyond Fundamental Rights in → Preamble (life, liberty: Art 3), Directive Principles (education: Art 26 → Art 45), Fundamental Duties (duties to community: Art 29).

35-033.r: Universal Declaration of Human Rights → adopted by UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948.

35-034.r: Universal Declaration of Human Rights → 30 Articles.
35-034.h: Think of a month: 30 days, 30 Articles.

35-035.r: 10 December → Human Rights Day (UDHR adopted 1948; UN resolution 423(V) in 1950). World Health Day → 7 April; UN Day → 24 October.

35-036.r: Concept of Human Rights → mainly emphasises dignity of man as a human being (UDHR Preamble: dignity and justice for all).

35-037.r: UDHR (10 December 1948) covers freedom and equality, life and liberty, education, and also privacy (no arbitrary interference); the exam key still marked right to privacy.
35-037.c: The book is wrong: the UDHR does protect privacy (no arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home or correspondence). All four options are in the UDHR; (d) is just the exam key.

35-038.r: UDHR (10 December 1948; 30 Articles; not legally binding) → no right to Universal Basic Income. Includes life, liberty, security (Art 3), adequate standard of living (Art 25).

35-039.r: Second-generation human rights → UDHR Arts 22 to 27, e.g., right to work (Art 23), right to education (Art 26). First generation → Arts 3 to 21.
35-039.c: No answer printed; both 'right to work' and 'right to education' are second-generation, so two options fit.

35-040.r: Eradication of social discrimination → second-generation human rights. First generation → civil and political (liberty); third → community and collective rights.
35-040.t: JPSC's key said third generation; the book holds second generation.

35-041.r: 'Right to the City' (Henri Lefebvre, 1968) → not an agreed human right (1 false); inhabitants' right to reclaim public spaces and participate; book marks statements 2 and 3 correct.
35-041.c: The explanation's line on unauthorised colonies contradicts its own answer; (d) 2 and 3 is the widely accepted answer.

35-042.r: Protection of Human Rights Ordinance, 1993 → issued by President under Article 123 on 28 September 1993, for NHRC, State Commissions and Human Rights Courts.

35-043.r: Protection of Human Rights Act → came into force in India on 28 September 1993.

35-044.r: Protection of Human Rights Act → in force from 28 September 1993; extends to the whole of India.
35-044.t: Option traps: 23 September and the year 1995; correct is 28 September 1993.

35-045.r: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 → set up National and State Human Rights Commissions and Human Rights Courts for better protection of human rights → all of the above.
